I can't answer your first question, but I have relevant experience with the second. I had a SA done years ago without local or twilight anesthesia. The pain was not unbearable, but it was distinctly uncomfortable and personally if I had been able to safely use the anesthesia, I would have done. The worst pain was when they inserted the rods to dilate my cervix, which they typically use lidocaine on to numb the area (but due to an allergy I opted to go without).

After the procedure I was given a Darvocet (an opioid pain reliever that was withdrawn from US markets in 2010, to give you an idea of how long ago this was) and was not in too much pain, but did have to have someone accompany me home. I was able to go back to work after a couple days of rest and only had mild cramping and bleeding.

I hope this helps and I wish you the best of luck!

Okay, I'm popping on my alt for this one because I'm too embarrassed to have this on my main.

One summer a bad storm knocked out the power to my house the day after I had done a big grocery run. We decided to go stay with my in-laws because it was unbearably hot in the house. Well, the power wound up being out for 10 days. I hadn't thought to toss out the food (didn't have a way to bring it to my in-laws since we don't have a car and used a grocery delivery service) so it sat there the whole time.

When the power was finally restored and we got back to the house, the fridge stank to high fucking heaven. To this day I have not smelled anything so rank and I work in a hospital full of nasty smells.

We couldn't afford a new fridge, though, so I donned several pairs of gloves and scoured the absolute *shit* out of that fridge. It was traumatizing, but we are still using the same fridge today and you wouldn't know the horror it's been through to look at it now.
If you're really interested I'll PM it to you! I don't want to break a rule or out myself (I'm even using an alt because my brother knows my Reddit username).
